definitions.explanation: The traditional, unsimplified forms of Chinese characters, still used in Taiwan, Hong Kong, and Macau. These are the original complex forms from which simplified characters were derived.

examples.japanese: {台湾|たいわん}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{繁体字|はんたいじ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{使|つか}われている→使う：00473_tsukau⟧。
examples.english: Traditional characters are used in Taiwan.

examples.japanese: {繁体字|はんたいじ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{画数|かくすう}→画数：13581_kakusuu⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{多|おお}くて→多い：01127_ooi⟧⟦{書|か}く→書く：00477_kaku⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{難|むずか}しい→難しい：00517_muzukashii⟧。
examples.english: Traditional characters have many strokes and are difficult to write.

examples.japanese: ⟦{日本|にほん}→日本：03876_nihon⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{漢字|かんじ}→漢字：09480_kanji⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{繁体字|はんたいじ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{近|ちか}い→近い：00530_chikai⟧もの⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{多|おお}い→多い：01127_ooi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧、⟦{独自|どくじ}→独自：05614_dokuji⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{略字|りゃくじ}⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: Many Japanese kanji are close to traditional characters, but there are also uniquely simplified forms.

notes:
USAGE:
Also called {正体字|せいたいじ} (standard-form characters) in Taiwan. Japanese kanji overlap significantly with traditional characters but are not identical — Japan carried out its own simplification reforms after World War II.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {繁体字|はんたいじ}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{書|か}く→書く：00477_kaku⟧: to write in traditional characters
- {繁体字|はんたいじ}⟦{圏|けん}→圏：21183_ken⟧: traditional character regions
- {繁体字|はんたいじ}⟦{表記|ひょうき}→表記：14123_hyouki⟧: traditional character notation
